components.name: Primary button
components.description: The inherited Mantine filled action: navigation blue at rest, blue.7 on hover. The default emphasis for a clear next step.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary">Continue</button>

components.name: Dark tool pill
components.description: Fully round, dark filled canvas action with a trailing icon (the Scan control). Reads as a tool over the map rather than a form action.

components.name: Discovery search
components.description: Large pill input (50px) with one 1px violet edge, set as the input's own border variable (violet.7 on light, violet.4 on dark) so focus still turns it to the primary color; while it holds text it ends with the shared ClearSearchButton. On the navigator it floats on the search-float shadow. The open list always says something: a loading line, dimmed busy results, "Nothing matches" with a hint and a Browse all tours option, or the failed request with Try again. A paid content's row carries the shared PaidMark. In the app a BorderAnimate wrapper runs a 4s border cycle around it; that is React-owned and not reproduced here.
components.html: The Long-Necked MadonnaRoom 4

components.name: Search-result card
components.description: The recurring calm container, implemented once as SearchResultCard (src/components/mantine/SearchResultCard.tsx): bordered card, md radius, sm shadow, 160px cover image, one-line title, two-line dimmed description, optional details below. SearchResultsGrid lays out tours, objects and contents results; variant="content" adds the 2px teal outline. With an optional href the title becomes a stretched link over the whole card and the shadow lifts to md on hover and focus-visible; tour and content results link to their page except while picking a tour stop.

The Long-Necked Madonna

Look at her very long neck: the painter stretched it on purpose, to make her look graceful.

The painting was never finished: a column on the right stands alone, without the rest of the building.

narrative.overview:
ArtAround should feel familiar and approachable to casual museum visitors as well as staff. Mantine is the main design system: recognizable controls, clear labels, system typography, neutral surfaces, and straightforward task flows provide the foundation. The existing UI is the main suggestion for the product's feel, but remains a prototype rather than a finished specification.

The system is best described as **one product over four namespaces**. They coexist in the same runtime and dress very different jobs:

1. **Visitor Mantine UI** — the visitor-facing interface. `src/theme.ts` is an empty `createTheme({})`, so the palette is Mantine's stock tokens plus Tailwind utilities; this layer is the brand authority for the visitor experience.
2. **shadcn / editor token layer** — Tailwind v4 `@theme inline` plus `:root` / `.dark` OKLCH variables (background, foreground, primary, border). Neutral by design; it is not Mantine's palette and should not be mistaken for it.
3. **Pascal editor and viewer** — the staff map editor and museum viewer, styled largely by `@pascal-app/*` module CSS and Tailwind `dark:` variants. Task-dense, dark-neutral, functionally layered.
4. **Assistance layer** — the voice assistant's look. Its shipped identity is the ember **assistant orb** (React Bits `CrystalizedBall`, `src/components/assistant/`), which sits in the tour-navigation bar. The older LiveKit `agents-ui` shader visualizers (cyan aura) remain in the code, but no screen renders them any more: only their session provider is still mounted in the frontend layout. Either way this namespace has exactly one sanctioned expression per screen (see Components → Assistant orb), not a global motif.

Playfulness belongs in small key components. Existing examples include the purple-to-orange tour carousel, the animated search border (the navigator home's one moving accent), the brand name's gradient in the home title, and selected discovery accents. These establish permission for selective expression; they do not require every page or control to animate or become decorative. Future refinement can improve consistency, spacing, accessibility, and responsive behavior while keeping this approachable character.
keyCharacteristics: Familiar and approachable Mantine controls as the visitor-facing foundation.
Neutral light and dark surfaces with clear task hierarchy.
Four coexisting style namespaces that must not be blended.
Small playful exceptions in museum discovery, scoped and few.
Functional depth for overlays and floating controls.
Generated help that wears the museum's own voice: buttons and forms, never a chat.
Prototype-informed direction with room for refinement.

rules.name: The Two-Namespace Rule
rules.body: Mantine color tokens and the editor's OKLCH tokens are distinct sources of truth in the incumbent code. Treat them as separate namespaces rather than one blended palette; do not "harmonize" one into the other as a side effect of a local change.

rules.name: The Scoped Playfulness Rule
rules.body: Decorative motion and gradient belong to named discovery components. If a playful treatment is being added to an ordinary form, list, or navigation element, it is out of scope by default.

rules.name: The Single Marker Table Rule
rules.body: Never pick a marker color locally. Add or change a marker kind in `markers.ts` so that the 2D chrome and the 3D material stay in sync.

rules.name: The Highlight-One Rule
rules.body: A chart colors exactly one series or bar: the visitor's own. Everything else is `chart-muted`. If nothing belongs to the viewer, the chart is single-hue.

rules.name: The Museum Primary Rule
rules.body: In museum mode (the museum switch, or a printed QR with `?museum=`) the navigation blue becomes the museum's color, and only it: buttons, links, active tab, selection, focus ring, the museum switch. Tour gradient, content teal, paid orange, difficulty, quiz feedback, markers, the destructive red and the accessibility blue (`accessibility-blue`, `ACCESSIBILITY_COLOR` in `src/theme.ts`: the museum's accessibility badge and feature checks, the tour's step-free badge, the map's wheelchair-route toggle) never change. The director picks one `brandColor`; `src/lib/museum-palette.ts` derives the 10 shades with Leonardo: a brand color with ≥ 4.5:1 on white is used as is for shade 6, a lighter one is darkened within its family until it reaches it; shade 9 stays ≥ 4.5:1 on shades 1–2. Saturated red and orange are refused (they already mean "delete" and "paid"); tour grape, content teal and Navigator green only warn. The scale is computed once per save and rendered on the server (`museumTheme` → `MantineProvider`), so there is no flash of blue. QR codes stay black on white.

rules.name: The Triplet Rule
rules.body: Difficulty and status are never carried by color alone. The incumbent renders label + icon + color together (`Leaf`/green, `Gauge`/yellow, `Flame`/red.9). Keep all three when restyling.

rules.name: The Gradient-Span Rule
rules.body: A gradient is applied to a fragment of text (a single word or short label) with `inherit` sizing, never to a paragraph. The navigator hero colors exactly one word this way, the app's name. Its stops are theme tokens per scheme, `light-dark(blue.7, blue.4)` → `light-dark(violet.7, violet.4)`, each above the 3:1 large text needs.

rules.name: The Below-md-Unchanged Rule
rules.body: A desktop adaptation is additive from `md` (62em). Gate it with Mantine's responsive props or an `md` media query; never change the phone layout for a desktop reason.

rules.name: The Thumb-Reach Rule
rules.body: Below `md`, on a focused task page, the next step lives full-width in the footer, inside reach of a standing visitor's thumb, and nowhere else. Content scrolls; the forward action does not. Build it with `ActionFooter` (`src/components/mantine/ActionFooter.tsx`): the 64px `AppShellFooter` with a `Container` matching the page column (`xs` for task pages, `sm` for the tour and content pages). From `md` there is no thumb to reach for: detail and outcome pages (tour, content, checkout) pass `inlineFrom="md"`: the footer steps aside and `ActionFooter` renders the same action inline where it is placed, right under what it acts on (`inlineProps` sizes and spaces it), so the action is written once. Step flows (the quiz, its results, the group quiz board) keep the footer at every width.

rules.name: The Navigation Reach Rule
rules.body: Navigation action targets are at least 44px; compact labels may keep their type scale while the hit area grows. Button labels wrap and their height grows with enlarged text. Bound secondary controls between the measured bars and let their column scroll; keep the essential command dock outside that scrolling column.

rules.name: The Overlay Opt-In Rule
rules.body: Floating controls over a map or canvas sit in a transparent, non-interactive overlay container; each control re-enables pointer events on itself. Never give the container pointer events back.

rules.name: The Functional-First Rule
rules.body: Shadows appear because something floats or overlays. Marketing-style ambient shadow on ordinary content is not part of the incumbent vocabulary.

rules.name: The Inherit-Radius Rule
rules.body: Nested surfaces take their radius from the parent (`rounded-[inherit]`) rather than inventing a new value; this is what keeps the `BorderAnimate` wrapper flush with the input it decorates.

rules.name: The Chart-Follows-Sentence Rule
rules.body: A chart never carries the takeaway alone. The sentence above it states the finding; the chart adds the distribution, and its container exposes a text summary for screen readers.

rules.name: The Edit-In-Place Rule
rules.body: Editing reuses the visitor's typography, spacing and Mantine controls. Don't introduce the neutral shadcn/editor layer or a dashboard look to visitor-facing pages because a form appeared on them.

rules.name: The Black-Code Rule
rules.body: QR codes are black on white with a 4-module quiet zone, error correction Q when printed, and never wear the museum color or a gradient: cameras read contrast, and a code must still scan in a dim room.

rules.name: The One Strip Rule
rules.body: Route status and the current direction share one slot in the navigation bar. A new route state becomes a state of the strip, never another banner in the footer.

rules.name: The One Crystal Rule
rules.body: The crystal/aura treatment belongs to the assistant orb and nowhere else. It is not background texture, not a card hover, and not a loading state. One orb per screen.

rules.name: The Mic-Closed-Looks-Calm Rule
rules.body: Only `listening` may look like it is hearing. If a change makes `ready` and `listening` hard to tell apart, the change is wrong.

rules.name: The Estimate-Looks-Lighter Rule
rules.body: The GPS estimate is always drawn lighter than the confirmed position (a translucent dot against the avatar), so nobody reads an estimate as the shareable position.

rules.name: The Same-Voice Rule
rules.body: Generated text wears the museum's own voice: no chat bubbles, avatars, typing cursor, word-by-word streaming, sparkle icon, "AI" wording or "generated" badge. It arrives one whole paragraph at a time, and only the metadata (`generation` groups in Payload) tells it apart from authored text.

rules.name: The Follow-the-Host Rule
rules.body: In a group, guests never get a control that would move them away from the host (steps, destinations, "go to" commands, scanner, position); they keep every control that only changes how they read or move (language, reading options, Tell me more, wheelchair route). Hide such controls; don't disable them. This covers the stepper (read-only progress), the step modal's "Go to next step", the object actions, the directions strip's "Take the quiz", and the quiz's "Back to the map".

rules.name: The Generated Size Rule
rules.body: Upload collections generate a `card` (480px) and a `cover` (1280px) size, never enlarged (`src/fields/imageUpload.ts`). Read pictures with `PICTURE_SELECT` and draw them with `pictureSrc(picture, 'card' | 'cover')` (`src/lib/picture.ts`), which falls back to the original. Only the lightbox draws the original.

rules.name: The Arrival and Discovery Rule
rules.body: Proximity suggestions stay inside the map's controls as a compact, scrollable, nonmodal surface. A next destination uses a flag, an explicit next-stop label and a filled primary action; an optional discovery uses a compass, a discovery label and a neutral action. Meaning must not depend on color alone. The filled action uses the deeper museum-primary shade with automatic text contrast. Recognition choices pair small images with names, with text/actions preserved when the image is missing. Opening an object and confirming “I am here” remain separate actions. No new design tokens were needed; the notice composes the existing Paper, Button and ActionIcon vocabulary.

rules.name: The Personal Reader Rule
rules.body: A family shares the works and host-led progress; each device chooses its own reader. The preview and group join reuse the labeled “Reading for” Select: Adult is the default, followed by the distinct planned child ages. Its description explains that language and detail change only on this device. Exact age remains in personal URL reading state across stops, versions and further explanations, never in shared group location state.

rules.name: The Museum Address Rule
rules.body: Use one Mantine address autocomplete with the provider's full postal label. Derive structured city from the selection; expose City only in the manual-location disclosure. Reuse MuseumLocationMap for public information and the editor draft, with a bounded one-pin map, readable address and recovery link. Save address and geographic point together. This extension adds no global tokens; existing Mantine fields and shared FormActions remain the design-system primitives.

rules.name: The Follow-the-System Rule
rules.body: The app is light or dark as the visitor's system says (`defaultColorScheme="auto"` in `AppMantineProvider` and `MantineColorSchemeScript`, set before the first paint). Tailwind's `dark:` follows the same `data-mantine-color-scheme` attribute (the `.dark` class stays for the Pascal editor). Text colored with a fixed dark shade (`c="green.8"`, `museum.8`, primary .8) is written `light-dark(<color>.8, <color>.4)` so it keeps AA on the dark page; filled buttons with `autoContrast` need nothing. `light-dark()` works in Mantine props (inline styles) and in Tailwind classes alike: Lightning CSS lowers the Tailwind ones to `--lightningcss-light/dark` variables, which `globals.css` sets from Mantine's attribute. In dark the theme lifts `dimmed` and the placeholder to dark.2/dark.1 mixes (about 4.8:1 and 4.6:1 on a card). The 3D map scene keeps its own light stage.

dos: **Do** use Mantine as the main visual foundation for visitor and staff task controls.
**Do** preserve an approachable feel for casual museum visitors.
**Do** keep the four namespaces distinct, and use semantic Mantine variables (`--mantine-color-*`) rather than hardcoding light surfaces.
**Do** confine playfulness to small named components where it helps discovery or feedback (see The Scoped Playfulness Rule).
**Do** keep content meaning available through labels and icons as well as color (see The Triplet Rule).

**Do** use the `museum` color (or no color) for the common action, so museum mode re-skins it; use `ACCESSIBILITY_COLOR` for anything that says "accessible", and plain `blue` only for markers (see The Museum Primary Rule).
**Do** keep QR codes black on white and build printed ones only through `/api/qr-sheet` (see The Black-Code Rule).
**Do** preserve explicit position confirmation, shareable modal URLs, and the Overlay Opt-In pattern when touching navigation.
**Do** source every museum-marker color and icon from `markers.ts` (see The Single Marker Table Rule).
**Do** pair paid orange with a `Lock`/`ShoppingBag` icon and a price or label, and keep navigation available beside any unlock action.
**Do** give every assistant capability a non-voice path: a command pill, an overlay control, or the directions modal.
**Do** show route states inside the directions strip, and transient guidance as top-center notifications.
**Do** offer generated help as named buttons, form fields and voice commands, and keep its state in the URL.
**Do** improve prototype inconsistencies, accessibility, and responsive behavior while preserving the intended feel.

**Do** put a focused task's single forward action full-width in the 64px footer below `md` (`ActionFooter`), with the content inside `AppShellMain`; from `md` detail and outcome pages pass `inlineFrom="md"`, which renders the same action inline where `ActionFooter` is placed, and only step flows keep the footer (see The Thumb-Reach Rule).
**Do** gate every desktop change at `md` and leave the phone layout as it is (see The Below-md-Unchanged Rule).

**Do** stick panes at `var(--site-pane-top)` and bound them with `var(--site-pane-height)`, and offset in-page sticky headers by `var(--site-header-height, 0px)`, so they sit under the site header on desktop and at the top on phones. Don't rewrite the calc inline: a bare `2 *` in a Mantine style prop becomes rem and breaks it.

**Do** build desktop detail pages as two Mantine `Grid` panes in the 1140px width, with the media or summary pane sticky where the other one scrolls; a page whose text is the point (content) keeps its reading column instead.
**Do** grade answers with color + icon + word, and keep graded options readable rather than disabled-gray.
**Do** state a chart's finding in a sentence first, and color only the viewer's own series (see The Highlight-One Rule).
**Do** build sign-in, sign-up and checkout outcomes from the existing planner column and focused-task patterns rather than new chrome.
**Do** show a checkout failure as text under the control that started it, and return the buyer to where the purchase began.
**Do** open a detail page with its `DetailCover`, and let it carry the pictures (lightbox) and the 3D model; draw pictures at a generated size (see The Generated Size Rule).
donts: **Don't** treat every prototype measurement, gradient, or animation in this file as an immutable brand requirement.
**Don't** turn ordinary forms and navigation into continuously animated showcases.
**Don't** confuse Mantine tokens with the separate Pascal/editor CSS-token layer.
**Don't** promote the orb's ember or the voice aura into a global motif, background, accent color, or loading treatment.
**Don't** draw the GPS estimate like the confirmed position, or add a compass: the map is always north-up.
**Don't** give group guests a disabled step or destination control; hide it (see The Follow-the-Host Rule).
**Don't** label generated text or tours as AI, add sparkles, chat bubbles or a typing effect, or open a free prompt box (see The Same-Voice Rule).
**Don't** present planned product capabilities or unverified accessibility compliance as implemented design evidence.
**Don't** treat the unused `shine-border`/`orbiting-circles` primitives, or the hardcoded search copy, as settled design.
**Don't** show disabled edit or delete controls to viewers who lack permission; omit them (see The Edit-In-Place Rule).
**Don't** wrap quiz review items or result sections in cards; use spacing, compact headings and dividers.
**Don't** add axes, grids or tooltips to small visitor-facing charts unless the reader needs to look up exact values.
**Don't** treat the `stripe-test` sandbox shop as a product pattern, or say a purchase is unlocked before the purchases collection confirms it.
**Don't** add another bottom-navigation entry until the 390px row stops truncating its labels.
**Don't** open the picture lightbox from inside a modal, or build a separate gallery beside the cover.
**Don't** show the site header on immersive surfaces (map navigation, scanner, map editor), or a second copy of the tabs' top row or bottom bar from `md`.
**Don't** dim or scroll-lock the map behind a contextual panel on desktop; dock it beside the map.
